newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open up 2.00 to 3.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open up 2.00 to 3.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 2.00 to 3.00 cents higher Monday as traders expected the market to bounce after Friday's weak finish.

New York arabica futures closed mainly lower Friday amid news of a settlement to a six-day truckers' strike in Colombia. Active July futures closed 4.95 cents at 193.25 cents a lb after setting a fresh contract high of 203.50 cents. Spot May finished down 3.40 at 216.35, while the outer months ended 4.30 lower to 6.00 higher.
Technically, traders pegged July nearby resistance at 195.00-196.00, then 200.00 cents and 203.50 cents, a contract high set on Friday. Support at Friday's low of 192.50 cents.
After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell 1,747 60-kg bags, to 48,603 bags as of April 24. There were 3,815 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.

The CFTC Commitment of Traders report for the two weeks ended April 22 showed non-commercial long positions rose by 950 lots, to 7,443 lots. Non-commercial short positions rose by 91 lots, to 840 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks fell by 3,083 lots, to 8,727 lots, while commercial short positions fell by 2,401 lots, to 18,495 lots.
Nonreportable long postions fell by 473 lots, to 12,203 lots and nonreportable short positions fell by 296 lots, to 9,038 lots.

LIFFE coffee futures were sharply lower early Monday, pressured by origin sales, but prices fell short of pre-opening expectations. At the midday break, July was off $20, to $1,608, after sinking to $1,595.
